definition_zh: 扭伤；关节扭伤；韧带扭伤
definition_en: an injury to a joint caused by a sudden twist, or to twist a joint so that its ligaments are stretched or torn
core_image: 脚掌踩实，脚踝却向外一歪，韧带被拉扯过度
scene: 篮球场上一次落地不稳，队医立刻跑进场内。He sprained his ankle when he landed after a jump shot.
sceneCN: 这里 sprain 是「扭伤」（第 1 个义项：突然扭转造成的关节韧带损伤）；句意：他跳投落地时扭伤了脚踝。

derivatives.zh: 由过去分词转成形容词，义为「扭伤的；因扭伤而受损的」
由现在分词转成动名词，义为「扭伤这一动作」

senses.title: A joint injury from a sudden twist
senses.definition: an injury to a joint caused by a sudden twist that stretches or tears its ligaments
senses.definitionCN: 关节因突然扭转而使韧带被拉伸或撕裂所造成的损伤
senses.example: A bad sprain kept her off the court for six weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 一次严重的扭伤让她六周没能上场。
senses.why: The Latin source means to press out, so a sprain is a joint pressed past its safe range.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语来源意为「挤出」，所以扭伤就是关节被挤出了安全的活动范围。

senses.title: To twist a joint and hurt it
senses.definition: to hurt a joint suddenly by twisting it beyond its normal range
senses.definitionCN: 突然把关节拧到正常活动范围之外而使其受伤
senses.example: He sprained his wrist while lifting the heavy box.
senses.exampleCN: 他搬那个重箱子时扭伤了手腕。
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb, naming the exact moment when the twist happens.
senses.whyCN: 名词转化为动词，指的正是那一下扭转发生的瞬间。

senses.title: A ligament injury graded by doctors
senses.definition: a clinical injury of the ligaments around a joint, often graded as mild, moderate, or severe
senses.definitionCN: 关节周围韧带的临床损伤，常分为轻度、中度与重度
senses.example: The doctor graded the ankle sprain as moderate.
senses.exampleCN: 医生把这次脚踝扭伤定为中度。
senses.why: Clinical use narrows the everyday twist to damage of the ligaments themselves.
senses.whyCN: 临床用法把日常的「扭一下」收窄为韧带本身的损伤。

senses.title: A painful twist that is not a broken bone
senses.definition: a painful joint injury that people treat at home because no bone is broken
senses.definitionCN: 人们在家处理的一种疼痛性关节损伤，因为骨头并没有断
senses.example: Rest and ice are enough for most sprains.
senses.exampleCN: 大多数扭伤只要休息和冰敷就够了。
senses.why: Everyday speech uses the word to separate a sprain from a fracture.
senses.whyCN: 日常说法用这个词把扭伤和骨折区分开来。

intro.en: Sprain traces back through Old French espreindre to Latin exprimere, to press out.
intro.cn: sprain 经古法语 espreindre 上溯到拉丁语 exprimere（挤出、压出）。

items.en: Exprimo, exprimere means to press or squeeze something out.
items.cn: exprimo、exprimere 意为把某物压出、挤出。

items.en: The participle expressus means pressed out, and it also feeds the word express.
items.cn: 分词 expressus 意为「被压出的」，它也是 express 的来源。

items.en: Espreindre means to press or squeeze, keeping the Latin image of pressure.
items.cn: espreindre 意为挤压，保留了拉丁语「加压」的意象。

items.en: Spraynen appears in the fourteenth century with the sense of wrenching a limb.
items.cn: spraynen 在十四世纪出现，义为猛扭肢体。

items.en: The verb sprain settles on the violent twist that hurts a joint.
items.cn: 动词 sprain 固定为「伤到关节的猛扭」。

items.en: The later noun sprain names the injury itself, not only the act.
items.cn: 较晚出现的名词 sprain 指损伤本身，而不只是动作。

note.en: Sprain sits beside strain and other twist words, and beside the clinical vocabulary of joint injuries.
note.cn: sprain 与 strain 等表示「拧、拉」的词相邻，也与关节损伤的临床词汇相邻。

entries.definition: to injure a muscle or tendon by overstretching it
entries.definitionCN: 拉伤肌肉或肌腱；只是拼写与 sprain 相近，词源不同
spring 的过去式；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: liquid sent through the air in tiny drops
entries.definitionCN: 喷雾；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a sudden turn that can hurt a joint
entries.definitionCN: 突然的扭转，可能伤到关节

entries.definition: to pull something apart by force

normalIntro.en: Sprain is a joint squeezed past its limit, and its forms and collocations are all regular.
normalIntro.cn: sprain 是关节被挤到限度之外，它的形式与搭配都很规则。

normal.en: Sprain and strain are different: a sprain damages ligaments, a strain damages muscles.
normal.cn: sprain 与 strain 不同：前者伤韧带，后者伤肌肉。

normal.en: An ankle sprain is one of the most common injuries in basketball.
normal.cn: 脚踝扭伤是篮球运动中最常见的损伤之一。

normal.en: The verb is regular, so the forms are sprains, sprained, and spraining.
normal.cn: 动词变化规则，形式为 sprains、sprained、spraining。

normal.en: Rest, ice, and a tight bandage help most sprains heal.
normal.cn: 休息、冰敷和绷带有助于大多数扭伤愈合。

normal.en: The Old French source meant to squeeze, and a sprain does squeeze a joint.
normal.cn: 古法语来源意为「挤压」，而扭伤正是把关节挤压了一下。

abstract.en: Picture an ankle rolling outward while the foot stays planted.
abstract.cn: 想象脚掌踩实，脚踝却向外一歪。

abstract.en: Imagine wringing a wet towel until the cloth twists tight.
abstract.cn: 想象拧一条湿毛巾，布被拧得紧紧的。

abstract.en: Think of a rubber band stretched to its limit but not snapped.
abstract.cn: 想象一根橡皮筋被拉到极限却还没崩断。

examples.en: She sprained her ankle during the warm-up.
examples.cn: 她在热身时扭伤了脚踝。

examples.en: A bad sprain can take six weeks to heal.
examples.cn: 严重的扭伤可能要六周才能痊愈。

examples.en: The coach wrapped the sprained wrist in tape.
examples.cn: 教练用胶布把扭伤的手腕缠了起来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「死拼」——带伤硬拼上场，落地一歪就扭伤；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 exprimere（挤出、压出）→ 古法语 espreindre（挤压）→ 中古英语 spraynen（猛扭）→ 英语 sprain，核心义「把关节挤到超出限度」。

sensesIntro.en: Sprain names the injury first, then the act of twisting, then clinical ligament damage, and finally the everyday injury that is not a break.
sensesIntro.cn: sprain 先指扭伤这一损伤，再指扭转的动作，继而指临床上的韧带损伤，最后指日常说的、并非骨折的扭伤。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an ankle rolling outward while the foot stays planted.
core.cn: 核心意象：脚掌落地时脚踝向外一歪。

branches.en: The injury noun is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 表示损伤的名词是日常义项。

branches.en: The verb names the twisting action itself.
branches.cn: 动词义项指扭转动作本身。

branches.en: Doctors grade ligament damage as a sprain.
branches.cn: 医生把韧带损伤分级称为扭伤。

branches.en: Everyday talk contrasts a sprain with a break.
branches.cn: 日常说法把扭伤与骨折作对照。

branches.en: The injury and the act are two sides of one event.
branches.cn: 损伤与动作是同一件事的两面。

intro.en: Sprain grows from the Latin verb exprimere, to press out, through Old French and Middle English.
intro.cn: sprain 从拉丁语动词 exprimere（挤出）经古法语与中古英语演变而来。

latinIntro.en: Latin ex- means out, and premere means to press, so exprimere means to press out.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ex- 表示「向外」，premere 表示「压」，exprimere 即「压出、挤出」。

items.example: The prefix marks movement outward.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标出向外的动作。

items.example: Premere supplies the pressing action.
items.exampleCN: premere 提供「压」的动作。

items.meaning: to press out, to squeeze out
items.example: The verb exprimere gives the squeezing image.
items.exampleCN: 动词 exprimere 提供挤压的意象。

items.example: The participle expressus means pressed out.
items.exampleCN: 分词 expressus 意为「被压出的」。

items.example: Old French espreindre carries the Latin pressure forward.
items.exampleCN: 古法语 espreindre 把拉丁语的「压」延续下来。

items.example: Middle English spraynen names a wrenching of the body.
items.exampleCN: 中古英语 spraynen 指猛扭身体。

items.meaning: a joint injury from a twist
items.example: The noun sprain names the injury itself.
items.exampleCN: 名词 sprain 指损伤本身。

items.meaning: to twist and injure a joint
items.example: The verb sprain names the act.
items.exampleCN: 动词 sprain 指这个动作。

items.example: The ending -ed forms sprained.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成 sprained。

items.example: The ending -ing forms spraining.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 spraining。

definition_en: to move a plant, organ, or piece of tissue from one place to another, or such a move
core_image: 一棵带土球的树被抬到新坑里，根须还带着旧地的泥
scene: 医院走廊里，护士推着装有捐献器官的保温箱快步走向手术室。The surgeons will transplant the donated kidney into the young patient.
sceneCN: 这里 transplant 是「移植」（第 1 个义项：把器官或组织移到另一个身体）；句意：外科医生将把这颗捐献的肾脏移植到这位年轻患者体内。

derivatives.zh: 动词加 -ation 构成名词，义为「移植；移植术」
动词加 -able 构成形容词，义为「可移植的」
动词加 -er 构成名词，义为「移栽者；移栽机」

senses.title: Moving an organ into another body
senses.definition: a medical operation that moves a healthy organ or tissue from one body to another
senses.definitionCN: 把健康的器官或组织从一个身体移到另一个身体的医疗手术
senses.example: The kidney transplant took five hours.
senses.exampleCN: 这台肾脏移植手术做了五个小时。
senses.why: Trans- means across and plantare means to plant, so the organ is planted in a new body.
senses.whyCN: trans- 意为「越过」，plantare 意为「栽种」，所以器官是被栽进一个新的身体。

senses.title: Replanting a plant in a new place
senses.definition: to dig up a growing plant and plant it again in another spot
senses.definitionCN: 把正在生长的植物挖起，再种到另一个地方
senses.example: We transplant the tomato seedlings in late spring.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在晚春移栽番茄幼苗。
senses.why: The oldest sense is agricultural: a plant is carried across and set into new soil.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项属于农业：植物被带过一段距离，安放进新的土壤。

senses.title: Moving people or things to a new place
senses.definition: to move a person, group, or thing to a different place or setting
senses.definitionCN: 把人、群体或事物移到另一个地方或环境
senses.example: The whole office was transplanted to a building near the river.
senses.exampleCN: 整个办公室被搬到了河边的一栋楼里。
senses.why: The agricultural image widens into any move that gives something a new setting.
senses.whyCN: 农业意象扩大为任何「给某物一个新环境」的迁移。

senses.title: A piece of living tissue moved by grafting
senses.definition: a piece of living tissue moved from one site to another, as in a skin graft
senses.definitionCN: 把一块活组织从一个部位移到另一个部位，如皮肤移植
senses.example: The burn unit used a skin transplant from the thigh of the patient.
senses.exampleCN: 烧伤科用患者大腿上的一块皮肤做了移植。
senses.why: A graft is a transplant on a small scale, moving living tissue from one site to another.
senses.whyCN: 移植物是小规模的移植，把活组织从一个部位挪到另一个部位。

intro.en: Transplant joins Latin trans, across, with plantare, to plant, and reaches English through French.
intro.cn: transplant 由拉丁语 trans（越过）与 plantare（栽种）组合，经法语进入英语。

items.en: Trans means across, beyond, or to the other side.
items.cn: trans 意为「越过、穿过、到另一边」。

items.en: Plantare means to plant, from planta, a shoot or the sole of the foot.
items.cn: plantare 意为栽种，源自 planta（幼苗；脚掌）。

items.en: Transplantare is recorded for planting something again elsewhere.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 transplantare 指把某物移种到别处。

items.en: French transplanter carries the word into gardening and, later, medicine.
items.cn: 法语 transplanter 把这个词带入园艺，后来又带入医学。

items.en: English transplant first names the moving of trees and plants.
items.cn: 英语 transplant 最初指搬运树木与植物。

items.en: Modern English extends transplant to organs, tissue, and whole communities.
items.cn: 现代英语把 transplant 扩展到器官、组织与整个群体。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the plantare family; the near-meaning group holds words for grafts, implants, and moves.
note.cn: 形近组收录 plantare 词族；近义组收录表示嫁接、植入与搬迁的词。

entries.definition: the act or operation of transplanting
to put a seed or young plant into the ground
entries.definitionCN: 把种子或幼苗种进土里

entries.definition: living tissue fixed onto another body or plant
entries.definitionCN: 嫁接到另一个身体或植物上的活组织

entries.definition: a device or tissue placed inside the body
entries.definitionCN: 植入体内的装置或组织

normalIntro.en: Transplant is a crossing plus a planting: something living is carried over and set down again.
normalIntro.cn: transplant 是「越过」加「栽种」：有生命的东西被带过去，再安放下来。

normal.en: Trans- means across and plantare means to plant, so a transplant crosses space to be planted.
normal.cn: trans- 意为「越过」，plantare 意为「栽种」，所以移植就是跨过一段距离去栽种。

normal.en: A heart transplant moves a healthy heart into a patient whose own heart is failing.
normal.cn: 心脏移植是把健康的心脏移入心脏衰竭的患者体内。

normal.en: Gardeners transplant seedlings when they outgrow the seed tray.
normal.cn: 幼苗长得超出育苗盘时，园丁就会移栽。

normal.en: The noun and the verb share one spelling: a transplant, to transplant.
normal.cn: 名词与动词拼写相同：a transplant 与 to transplant。

normal.en: Do not confuse transplant with implant: an implant is placed inside, a transplant arrives from another body.
normal.cn: 别把 transplant 与 implant 混淆：implant 是放入体内，transplant 来自另一个身体。

abstract.en: Picture a donor organ carried in a cold box into a new body.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗捐献器官装在冷藏箱里，被送进一个新的身体。

abstract.en: Imagine a seedling lifted with its roots and set into fresh soil.
abstract.cn: 想象一株幼苗连根被捧起，放进新鲜的土里。

abstract.en: Think of a whole office packed up and reopened in another city.
abstract.cn: 想象整个办公室被打包，在另一座城市重新开张。

examples.en: The hospital performed a heart transplant last night.
examples.cn: 这家医院昨晚做了一台心脏移植手术。

examples.en: Farmers transplant rice seedlings in early summer.
examples.cn: 农民在初夏移栽水稻秧苗。

examples.en: The transplanted tissue was accepted by the patient.
examples.cn: 移植的组织被患者接受了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「穿石烂种」——把苗穿过石缝硬栽下去，居然活了；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 trans-（越过、穿过）+ plantare（栽种，源自 planta「幼苗；脚掌」）→ 中世纪拉丁语 transplantare → 英语 transplant，核心义「连根带土挪到别处栽下」。

sensesIntro.en: Transplant moves from plants to organs, then widens to people and things, and finally narrows to a graft of tissue.
sensesIntro.cn: transplant 从植物移栽出发，转向器官移植，再扩大到人与物的迁移，最后收窄为组织移植。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tree with its root ball carried to a new pit.
core.cn: 核心意象：一棵带着土球的树被抬到新坑里。

branches.en: The organ sense is the medical branch.
The plant sense is the oldest branch.
branches.cn: 植物义项是最古老的分支。

branches.en: The moving sense covers people and things.
The tissue sense is a small-scale graft.
branches.cn: 组织义项是小规模的移植。

branches.en: Both move living material into another body or site.
branches.cn: 两者都把活体材料移入另一个身体或部位。

intro.en: Transplant is built from the Latin prefix trans- and the verb plantare, with English derivatives around it.
intro.cn: transplant 由拉丁语前缀 trans- 与动词 plantare 构成，周围有一组英语派生词。

latinIntro.en: Latin trans means across, and plantare means to plant, from planta, a shoot.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 trans 意为「越过」，plantare 意为「栽种」，源自 planta（幼苗）。

items.example: The prefix marks a crossing from one place to another.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标出从一处到另一处的跨越。

items.example: Plantare supplies the planting action.
items.exampleCN: plantare 提供「栽种」的动作。

items.meaning: a shoot, a sprout, the sole
items.example: Planta is the noun behind plantare.
items.exampleCN: planta 是 plantare 背后的名词。

items.example: Transplantare joins the prefix and the verb.
items.exampleCN: transplantare 把前缀与动词连在一起。

items.example: French transplanter passes the compound to English.
items.exampleCN: 法语 transplanter 把这个复合词传给英语。

items.example: The verb transplant names the move.
items.exampleCN: 动词 transplant 指这一移动。

items.meaning: an organ or plant moved elsewhere
items.meaningCN: 移植的器官；移栽的植株
items.example: The noun transplant names the thing moved.
items.exampleCN: 名词 transplant 指被移走的东西。

items.example: The suffix -ation forms transplantation.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ation 构成 transplantation。

items.example: It turns a verb into a noun of action.
items.exampleCN: 它把动词变成表示动作的名词。

items.example: The suffix -able forms transplantable.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -able 构成 transplantable。

definition_zh: 物理治疗；理疗；康复治疗
definition_en: the treatment of injury or disease by physical methods such as exercise, massage, heat, and electricity rather than by drugs or surgery
core_image: 治疗师扶着病人的小腿，一点点把膝盖弯到能重新走路的角度
scene: 康复室里，治疗师扶着病人慢慢抬起小腿，墙上挂着训练计划。After the knee operation, she went to physiotherapy three times a week.
sceneCN: 这里 physiotherapy 是「物理治疗」（第 1 个义项：用运动、按摩、热疗等物理手段治疗）；句意：膝盖手术后，她每周去做三次物理治疗。

derivatives.zh: 由 physiotherapy 加 -ist 构成，义为「物理治疗师」
由 physiotherapy 加 -ic 构成，义为「物理治疗的」
physiotherapy 的口语缩略形式，义为「理疗；物理治疗师」

senses.title: Treatment by physical methods
senses.definition: treatment of pain or injury with movement, massage, heat, or electric currents rather than drugs
senses.definitionCN: 用运动、按摩、热疗或电流而不是药物来治疗疼痛或损伤
senses.example: Physiotherapy began two days after the operation.
senses.exampleCN: 手术两天后就开始做物理治疗。
senses.why: Physis means nature and therapeia means healing, so the cure works with natural forces.
senses.whyCN: physis 意为「自然」，therapeia 意为「治疗」，所以这种疗法顺着自然之力起效。

senses.title: The profession and its service
senses.definition: the profession or clinic service that provides such treatment
senses.definitionCN: 提供这种治疗的专业或诊所服务
senses.example: The team includes a physiotherapy department and two assistants.
senses.exampleCN: 这个团队包括一个物理治疗科和两名助手。
senses.why: A method of treatment also names the profession that delivers it.
senses.whyCN: 一种治疗方法也会用来命名提供它的专业。

senses.title: A planned course of treatment
senses.definition: a planned series of sessions of such treatment
senses.definitionCN: 按计划进行的一系列此类治疗
senses.example: The doctor referred her for a course of physiotherapy.
senses.exampleCN: 医生转介她去做一个疗程的物理治疗。
senses.why: The uncountable method is counted into sessions, giving a course of treatment.
senses.whyCN: 不可数的疗法被按次数计数，就成了一个疗程。

senses.title: Rehabilitation after injury or surgery
senses.definition: the work of restoring movement and strength after an injury or an operation
senses.definitionCN: 在受伤或手术后恢复活动能力与力量的工作
senses.example: Physiotherapy restored the full range of motion in his shoulder.
senses.exampleCN: 物理治疗让他肩膀的活动范围完全恢复了。
senses.why: The natural image turns into a practical goal: the body is guided back to its own power.
senses.whyCN: 「自然」的意象落成一个实际目标：引导身体回到自身的力量。

intro.en: Physiotherapy joins Greek physis, nature, with therapeia, healing, in a modern medical coinage.
intro.cn: physiotherapy 把希腊语 physis（自然）与 therapeia（治疗）组合成一个现代医学术语。

items.en: Physis means nature or the natural order of a thing.
items.cn: physis 意为「自然」或事物的自然秩序。

items.en: Therapeia means service, attendance, or healing.
items.cn: therapeia 意为「侍奉、照料、治疗」。

items.en: Physica, the Latin title of works on nature, carries physis into learned English.
items.cn: physica 是论自然的著作的拉丁语标题，把 physis 带入学术英语。

items.en: Therapia is the Latinized form of therapeia used in medical writing.
items.cn: therapia 是 therapeia 在医学写作中使用的拉丁化形式。

items.en: Nineteenth-century medicine coins physiotherapy from the two Greek roots.
items.cn: 十九世纪的医学从这两个希腊词根造出 physiotherapy。

items.en: The word spreads with the growth of rehabilitation after the World Wars.
items.cn: 随着两次世界大战后康复事业的发展，这个词传播开来。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the therapy family; the near-meaning group holds rehabilitation and body-work words.
note.cn: 形近组收录 therapy 词族；近义组收录康复与身体手法相关的词。

entries.definition: a person trained to give physiotherapy
entries.definitionCN: 受过训练、提供物理治疗的人

entries.definition: the informal short form of physiotherapy
the process of restoring health and function
entries.definitionCN: 恢复健康与功能的过程

entries.definition: rubbing and kneading the body to relieve pain
treatment by adjusting the bones of the spine
entries.definitionCN: 通过调整脊椎来治疗的方法

normalIntro.en: Physiotherapy is nature plus healing: the body is treated by movement, touch, heat, and current.
normalIntro.cn: physiotherapy 是「自然」加「治疗」：用运动、手法、热与电流来对待身体。

normal.en: Physio- comes from Greek physis, nature, and -therapy from therapeia, healing.
normal.cn: physio- 来自希腊语 physis（自然），-therapy 来自 therapeia（治疗）。

normal.en: A physiotherapist teaches exercises instead of prescribing pills.
normal.cn: 物理治疗师教你做练习，而不是开药。

normal.en: Physiotherapy is common after a knee or shoulder operation.
normal.cn: 膝盖或肩膀手术后常要做物理治疗。

normal.en: In speech, physiotherapy is often shortened to physio.
normal.cn: 口语里 physiotherapy 常缩略为 physio。

normal.en: Physiotherapy and drug therapy differ: one uses movement, the other uses medicine.
normal.cn: 物理治疗与药物治疗不同：一个用运动，一个用药。

abstract.en: Picture a therapist guiding a stiff knee through a slow bend.
abstract.cn: 想象治疗师托着僵硬的膝盖，慢慢把它弯下去。

abstract.en: Imagine a clinic room with mats, weights, and a treatment table.
abstract.cn: 想象一间诊室，里面有垫子、哑铃和治疗床。

abstract.en: Think of a calendar with two sessions marked each week.
abstract.cn: 想象一张日历，每周都标着两次治疗。

examples.en: She had physiotherapy for six weeks after the accident.
examples.cn: 事故之后，她做了六周物理治疗。

examples.en: Physiotherapy helped him walk without crutches.
examples.cn: 物理治疗帮助他不用拐杖走路。

examples.en: The clinic offers physiotherapy for sports injuries.
examples.cn: 这家诊所为运动损伤提供物理治疗。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「肺舒疗」——把身体舒展开、让肿痛消散的疗法；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 physis（自然、本性）+ therapeia（照料、治疗）→ 拉丁语 physica 与中世纪拉丁语 therapia 保留两个词根 → 十九世纪英语合成 physiotherapy，核心义「顺着身体本性，用运动与手法帮助恢复」。

sensesIntro.en: Physiotherapy first names a method, then the profession, then a counted course, and finally the rehabilitation it delivers.
sensesIntro.cn: physiotherapy 先指一种疗法，再指这门专业，继而指可计数的疗程，最后指它带来的康复。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a therapist guiding a stiff joint back into motion.
core.cn: 核心意象：治疗师引导僵硬的关节重新动起来。

branches.en: The method sense is the medical core.
The profession sense names the people and the clinic.
The course sense counts the sessions.
branches.cn: 疗程义项把治疗按次数计算。

branches.en: The rehabilitation sense names the goal.
The method exists to bring the body back to movement.
branches.cn: 方法的存在就是为了让身体重新动起来。

intro.en: Physiotherapy is built from two Greek roots, physis and therapeia, joined in modern medical language.
intro.cn: physiotherapy 由两个希腊词根 physis 与 therapeia 构成，在现代医学语言里合成。

latinIntro.en: Latin physica and Medieval Latin therapia carried the two Greek roots into European medical writing.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 physica 与中世纪拉丁语 therapia 把这两个希腊词根带入欧洲医学写作。

items.example: Physis gives the first half of the word.
items.exampleCN: physis 提供这个词的前半部分。

items.example: Therapeia gives the therapy half.
items.exampleCN: therapeia 提供 therapy 这一半。

items.example: The form physio- begins the compound.
items.exampleCN: 构词成分 physio- 位于复合词开头。

items.example: The form -therapy ends many medical words.
items.exampleCN: 构词成分 -therapy 出现在许多医学词末尾。

items.example: The compound names the method.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词命名该方法。

items.example: The suffix -ist marks the person.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ist 标出从事的人。

items.example: The suffix -ic forms the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ic 构成形容词。

items.example: Speech shortens the long compound to physio.
items.exampleCN: 口语把长复合词缩短为 physio。

items.example: It turns the method into a profession name.
items.exampleCN: 它把疗法变成职业名称。

items.example: It turns the noun into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它把名词变成形容词。
